extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders and members of the public who wish to comment on EPA pesticide registration actions (e.g., growers, applicators, farmworkers, public health professionals, environmental advocates)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting public comments on EPA pesticide registration and related regulatory actions under FIFRA and FFDCA, including what to include in effective comments and when opportunities to comment arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory triggers for public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) and Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FFDCA) require EPA to engage the public at specific times during the registration process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of statutory triggers include: when EPA receives an application for registration of a new pesticide active ingredient or one that would entail a changed use pattern; and when EPA is issuing notices related to tolerance changes or cancellation orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA sets specific comment period lengths depending on the type of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For actions related to biopesticide active ingredients, EPA offers a 15-day comment period (or 30 days when appropriate). For most conventional pesticides, EPA announces a 30-day comment period. Fifteen-day periods apply when a low risk active ingredient is involved, reduced risk status is granted, or the pesticide is proposed for IR-4-supported minor uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional engagement opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA offers additional opportunities for public engagement beyond the initial comment periods required by FIFRA and FFDCA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public input beyond statutory comment windows is encouraged because it helps inform risk assessment and risk management. Check dockets and EPA announcements for supplemental engagement opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify yourself
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting comments for FIFRA registration/registration review, clearly identify who you are (e.g., grower, applicator, farmworker, public health professional, environmental advocate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing your role or affiliation helps EPA understand the perspective and potential exposure patterns relevant to your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific application or use patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Include references to specific application/use patterns in your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify how and where the pesticide is or would be used (crop types, application methods, timing) so EPA can relate concerns to realistic exposure scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference EPA's risk assessment documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage directly with EPA's risk assessment documents in your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to particular findings, assumptions, or data gaps in EPA's assessments to make your comment actionable and focused on the agency's analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide use data (rates, frequency, geography)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply empirical use data such as application rates, frequency, and geographic distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete use data helps EPA refine exposure estimates and risk characterizations. Indicate data sources and any supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite peer-reviewed toxicology studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Support comments with citations to peer-reviewed toxicology literature when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full citations or copies of studies, and explain how the findings relate to EPA's assessments or regulatory decision points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Endocrine Disruptor Screening Program (EDSP) data
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss EDSP-related data and implications where relevant to the chemical's hazard profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether EDSP data support, contradict, or leave unresolved potential endocrine-related effects and how EPA should consider such data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with Endangered Species Act consultation considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and comment on aspects relevant to Endangered Species Act (ESA) consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address potential impacts on listed species or habitats and reference any species-specific exposure pathways or ecological data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address farmworker exposure and Worker Protection Standard issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly address farmworker exposure concerns and Worker Protection Standard (WPS) implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail exposure scenarios for workers, potential gaps in protections, and any recommended changes to labeling or practices to reduce risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference dietary exposure assessments and tolerance levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss dietary exposure assessments and existing or proposed tolerances/exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link comments to EPA's dietary exposure modeling, tolerance decisions, and whether current tolerances are protective based on available data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address resistance management
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise concerns or evidence about pesticide resistance management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe observed resistance patterns, monitoring data, and suggested stewardship or resistance mitigation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with alternatives (IPM, organic, mechanical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss feasible alternatives to the pesticide, such as integrated pest management (IPM), organic options, or mechanical controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information on effectiveness, availability, and comparative risks/benefits of alternatives to support EPA's risk management decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note pollinator impacts where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Include information on potential pollinator impacts when pertinent to the pesticide or use pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite studies, field observations, or monitoring data regarding pollinator exposure and effects, and suggest mitigation measures if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite USDA NASS data on pesticide use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) data as a source for pesticide use information when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference specific NASS datasets or tables to support claims about usage patterns, acreage treated, or trends over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stages when comments are solicited
rubrics_metrics.description: There are multiple stages during which the public may comment on registration-related matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These stages include: public comment on registration applications; registration review docket comments (every 15 years per active ingredient); special review and reregistration eligibility decisions; and tolerance and exemption rulemakings. Submit comments at the appropriate stage/docket for greatest relevance.
